Initial State

Initial State defines how a FeatureCell obtains its first authoritative value. Initialization is a deterministic, single-pass operation that executes through the full pipeline as a replaceState operation.

A FeatureCell does not assume state. It must be explicitly initialized through one of four intentional configuration mechanisms. Vault does not introduce fallback behavior, hierarchical rescue, or implicit retries.

  • hydrate() — Provide a deferred factory (synchronous or asynchronous) that resolves to the authoritative initial value. This is treated as the primary initialization source when declared.
  • Persist Behaviors — Install one or more Persist behaviors that load previously stored state (e.g., localStorage, sessionStorage, or custom storage providers). The first defined value becomes the initialization candidate.
  • descriptor.initialState — Supply a static initial value directly in the FeatureCell descriptor. This value is used only when no hydrate() or Persist behaviors are declared.
  • Explicit replaceState() — Omit all automatic initialization mechanisms and programmatically initialize the FeatureCell after creation using replaceState().
Note

Initialization failures should be treated as catastrophic correctness violations. If the declared initialization source does not produce the expected value, the FeatureCell does not silently recover. Recovery is always explicit.

Why Initialization Failure Is Considered Catastrophic

Initialization defines the starting contract of a FeatureCell. If that contract fails, the pipeline remains operational — but your application logic may now execute against an invalid or unexpected state shape.

Vault does not automatically fall back, retry silently, or substitute alternate state sources. The declared initialization mechanism represents intentional engineer configuration. If it fails, the resulting state does not match the declared expectation.

Examples of downstream impact:

  • If you expected an array and received undefined, reducers may attempt to push into a non-existent structure.
  • If you expected hydrated API data, UI components may render incomplete or empty views.
  • If you expected persisted state, user workflows may branch incorrectly.
  • If you expected a populated dropdown, it may render empty while the rest of the application continues executing.

For this reason, initialization failure is considered catastrophic from a correctness perspective. The system is still running — but your assumptions are no longer aligned with runtime reality.

When initialization fails:

  • The error is surfaced locally and optionally globally.
  • The state remains value: undefined with hasValue: false.
  • No implicit fallback or recovery occurs.

Recommended Recovery Pattern

If recovery is desired, it must be explicit:

  1. Call reset() to clear the failed initialization attempt.
  2. Provide a known-good value using replaceState().

Recovery is intentional, observable, and deterministic. Vault does not guess.

Example: How to Recover from Initialization Failure

{{`@FeatureCell<Employee[]>('employees')
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class EmployeeService {
  private isInitializationAttempted = false;
  private readonly vault = injectVault<Employee[]>(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    effect(() => {
      const error = this.vault.state.error();

      if (error) {
        console.error('Initialization failed:', error);

        if (!this.isInitializationAttempted) {
          // Step 1: Reset the FeatureCell to clear the error state
          this.vault.reset();

          // Step 2: Explicitly replace state with a known-good value
          const fallbackEmployees: Employee[] = [
            { id: 1, name: 'Alice' },
            { id: 2, name: 'Bob' }
          ];

          this.vault.replaceState({ value: fallbackEmployees });
        }
      }

      this.isInitializationAttempted = true;
    });

    this.vault
      .hydrate(() => Promise.resolve(...))
      .initialize();
  }
}`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<Employee[]>(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: [],
  }
);

let isInitializationAttempted = false;

employeeCell.state$.subscribe({ next(state) => {
  if (state.error) {
    console.error('Initialization failed:', state.error);
    if (!isInitializationAttempted) {

      // Step 1: Reset the FeatureCell to clear the error state
      employeeCell.reset();

      // Step 2: Explicitly replace state with a known-good value
      const fallbackEmployees: Employee[] = [
        { id: 1, name: 'Alice' },
        { id: 2, name: 'Bob' }
      ];

      employeeCell.replaceState({ value: fallbackEmployees });
    } else {
      // Handle subsequent errors after recovery attempt (optional)
    }
  }

  // Handle normal state updates here
  isInitializationAttempted = true;
});

employeeCell.hydrate(() => Promise.resolve()).initialize();

`}}

Diagram
Design Decisions

FeatureCell initialization is intentionally strict. Initialization integrates into the deterministic pipeline model and does not introduce fallback layers, implicit retries, or hierarchical rescue behavior. The table below documents how initialization responds to specific runtime conditions.

Initialization Design Decisions
Condition Behavior
hydrate() Declared hydrate() is treated as the authoritative initialization source. Persist behaviors and descriptor.initialState are not evaluated. The resolved value is passed through the full pipeline as a replaceState operation.
Persist Behaviors Present (No hydrate) Persist behaviors are evaluated sequentially. The first defined value becomes the initialization candidate and executed as a replaceState operation. descriptor.initialState is not evaluated.
descriptor.initial Only When neither hydrate() nor Persist behaviors are configured, descriptor.initialState is treated as the authoritative static value and executed as a replaceState operation.
Undefined Resolution If the selected initialization source resolves to undefined, no write occurs. The FeatureCell state value remains as undefined with hasValue = false. This is not treated as an error.
Initialization Source Throws A thrown error during hydrate() or Persist loading is treated as an initialization failure. No fallback source is evaluated. The error is emitted and the state remains undefined.
No Initialization Mechanism Declared The FeatureCell begins with value = undefined and must be explicitly initialized via replaceState(). This is considered a valid intentional configuration.
Initialization Failure Recovery Recovery is explicit. The engineer must call reset() and then replaceState(). Initialization does not automatically retry and no implicit fallback occurs.
Initialization Mechanisms

A FeatureCell may be initialized in exactly one of the following ways:

  • 1. hydrate() — Deferred factory resolution (highest precedence)
  • 2. Persisted Storage — Installed Persist behaviors
  • 3. descriptor.initialState — Static configuration value
  • 4. Manual replaceState() — Explicit runtime initialization

Only one source provides the initial value during a single initialization cycle. These sources are not fallback layers. They are mutually exclusive declarations of intent.

Why hydrate() has highest precedence: The hydrate() mechanism is evaluated first because it represents an explicit request for dynamic, authoritative data. When an engineer declares hydrate(), they are intentionally choosing runtime-derived state (API responses, deferred computation, remote data, etc.) over static configuration or previously persisted storage. In that case, persisted data is considered stale and descriptor-based initial values are irrelevant.

Note

If dynamic data is not desired, do not use hydrate(). Vault will then resolve initialization using storage or static configuration instead.

1. hydrate() — Deferred Initialization

Calling hydrate() declares that the authoritative initial state must be resolved from a deferred factory. This factory may return a value synchronously or resolve asynchronously via Promise.

If hydrate() is configured, it always executes first. Storage and static initial values are not evaluated.

If the deferred factory:

  • Resolves to a value → The pipeline executes a Replace.
  • Resolves to undefined → No write occurs. State remains undefined.
  • Throws → Initialization fails.

A thrown error is treated as an initialization failure because the declared authoritative source did not resolve successfully.

hydrate() is a core fluent API method provided by the FeatureCell itself. It does not require any additional Behaviors to be registered on the FeatureCell declaration. The Resolve stage already includes built-in support for deferred factories and Promise-based inputs. When you call hydrate(), you are using a first-class initialization mechanism that integrates directly with the pipeline without installing custom resolve logic.

Example: How to configure .hydrate()

{{`@FeatureCell<Employee[]>('employees')
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class EmployeeService {
  private readonly vault = injectVault<Employee[]>(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    this.vault
      .hydrate(() => Promise.resolve(...))
      .initialize();
  }
}`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<Employee[]>(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    // ignored
    initialState: []
  }
);

employeeCell.hydrate(() => Promise.resolve(...)).initialize();

`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<Employee[]>(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    // ignored
    initialState: []
  }
);

employeeCell.hydrate(() => Promise.resolve(...)).initialize();

`}}
2. Persisted Storage — Persist Behaviors

If one or more Persist behaviors are registered on the FeatureCell declaration and hydrate() is not configured, Vault attempts to load state from storage.

Persist behaviors must be explicitly registered on the FeatureCell. Storage loading is not automatic. If no Persist behavior is installed, this initialization path is skipped entirely.

Persist behaviors are evaluated sequentially. The first defined value returned becomes the initial state candidate.

  • Value returned → The pipeline executes replaceState.
  • undefined or null returned → No write occurs. The state remains undefined.
  • Thrown error → Initialization fails.

This mechanism assumes a value actually exists in storage. If storage contains no entry, the Persist behavior simply returns undefined (or null), and no state write is performed.

If a Persist behavior throws during load, initialization is considered failed. Vault does not fall back to descriptor.initialState.

Example: How to configure storage initialization

{{`// app.config.ts

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    provideVault({ logLevel: 'off' }),

    provideFeatureCell(
      EmployeeService
      {  
        key: 'employees',
        // ignored
        initialState: []
      },
      [
        withLocalStorageBehavior, 
      ]
    )
  ]
};

@FeatureCell<Employee[]>('employees')
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class EmployeeService {
  private readonly vault = injectVault<Employee[]>(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    this.vault.initialize();
  }
}`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<Employee[]>(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    // ignored
    initialState: []
  }
);

employeeCell.initialize();

`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<Employee[]>(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    // ignored
    initialState: []
  }
);

employeeCell.initialize();

`}}
3. descriptor.initialState — Static Configuration

If neither Fluent API hydrate() method is configured nor Persist behaviors are registered with the FeatureCell, the static initialState value declared in the FeatureCell descriptor is evaluated.

This value is treated as authoritative and immediately passed through the pipeline as a Replace operation.

If initialState is undefined, no write occurs and the FeatureCell begins with an undefined state.

Example: How to configure descriptor.initialState initialization

{{`// app.config.ts

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    provideVault({ logLevel: 'off' }),

    provideFeatureCell(
      EmployeeService
      {  
        key: 'employees',
        // Initial state is declared directly in the descriptor
        initialState: [
          { id: 1, name: 'Alice' },
          { id: 2, name: 'Bob' }
        ]
      }
    )
  ]
};

@FeatureCell<Employee[]>('employees')
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class EmployeeService {
  private readonly vault = injectVault<Employee[]>(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    this.vault.initialize();
  }
}`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<Employee[]>(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    // Initial state is declared directly in the descriptor
    initialState: [
      { id: 1, name: 'Alice' },
      { id: 2, name: 'Bob' }
    ]
  },
);

employeeCell.initialize();

`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<Employee[]>(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    // Initial state is declared directly in the descriptor
    initialState: [
      { id: 1, name: 'Alice' },
      { id: 2, name: 'Bob' }
    ]
  },
);

employeeCell.initialize();

`}}
4. Manual replaceState() — Explicit Runtime Initialization

An engineer may choose not to declare hydrate(), Persist behaviors, or descriptor.initialState.

In this case, the FeatureCell begins with:

  • hasValue: false
  • isLoading: false
  • value: undefined
  • error: null

The engineer must then explicitly call replaceState() to establish the initial value.

This is a valid and intentional initialization strategy.

Note

When performing manual initialization, you should use replaceState(), not mergeState(). At this point the FeatureCell has no existing value. Using mergeState() would attempt to merge onto undefined, which may reproduce the same incorrect assumptions that led to the missing initial state. replaceState() establishes a clean, authoritative baseline and ensures downstream logic operates on a fully defined value.

Example: How to configure initialization with replaceState()

{{`// app.config.ts

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    provideVault({ logLevel: 'off' }),

    provideFeatureCell(
      EmployeeService
      {  
        key: 'employees',
        // ignored as undefined
        initialState: undefined
      },
    )
  ]
};

@FeatureCell<Employee[]>('employees')
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class EmployeeService {
  private readonly vault = injectVault<Employee[]>(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    this.vault.initialize();

    this.vault.replaceState({
      value : [
          { id: 1, name: 'Alice' },
          { id: 2, name: 'Bob' }
      ]
    });
  }
}`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<Employee[]>(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    // ignored as undefined
    initialState: undefined
  }
);

employeeCell.initialize();

employeeCell.replaceState({
  value : [
      { id: 1, name: 'Alice' },
      { id: 2, name: 'Bob' }
  ]
});

`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<Employee[]>(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    // ignored as undefined
    initialState: undefined
  }
);

employeeCell.initialize();

employeeCell.replaceState({
  value : [
      { id: 1, name: 'Alice' },
      { id: 2, name: 'Bob' }
  ]
});

`}}
Initialization Execution Model

Initialization is not a direct state mutation. It is enqueued into the Conductor and executed as a standard pipeline replaceState operation.

This guarantees:

  • Deterministic ordering
  • Serialized pipeline execution
  • Full DevTools trace visibility
  • Consistent reducer and behavior participation

Initialization passes through the same Resolve, Operator, Filter, Reducer, and Emit stages as any other replaceState operation.

Because initialization is processed through the full pipeline, any installed interceptors, operators, filters, or reducers may transform, suppress, or reject the initial state candidate. If a value does not ultimately commit to state, Vault does not treat that as an initialization failure — it is behaving exactly as configured. In this case, you as the engineer must recognize that the candidate you submitted was intentionally altered or filtered out by your own pipeline logic.

Failure Model

Initialization failure occurs only when a declared initialization source throws an error.

Undefined resolution is not failure.

On initialization failure:

  • hasValue remains false
  • isLoading becomes false
  • value remains undefined
  • error is populated as a VaultErrorShape

The pipeline remains operational, but the initialization cycle is considered catastrophic because declared expectations were violated.

Vault does not retry. Vault does not fall back. Vault does not rescue implicitly.

Recovery

Recovery from initialization failure is explicit.

The engineer must:

  1. Call reset()
  2. Invoke replaceState() with a valid value

Initialization does not automatically re-run. No fallback source is evaluated.
